resources.string: The fonts were applied, but the font service did not reload them. Open TypeFace Droplet to restart the system softly.
The fonts could not be applied after the boot: %1$s
Replacing the system fonts requires root. None of the following can provide it right now:

Shizuku runs through ADB (as the shell user). The shell user cannot change system mounts or the components of other applications, so fonts cannot be applied. Start Shizuku with root, or use Sui or su.
This application has not been granted access yet.
The installed version is too old.
The state of the system is not known yet.
The state of the system can be read once a privilege is available.
The guard is watching the system after the reload.
The guard restored the original configuration because the system crashed after a reload: %1$s. Automatic application at boot is paused until you apply manually.
Applied: %1$d families replaced. Applications started from now on use the new fonts; applications that are already running keep their fonts until they restart.

The documents were replaced, but the font service of this system did not reload them (it reloads only on systems with fs-verity). A soft restart restarts every application and the system services, without rebooting the device.
No rule matched any font family of this system, so nothing changed.
The original fonts are back. Applications that are running keep the replacement fonts until they restart.

su runs this application as root, but the root manager has removed the capabilities of root, so fonts can be neither applied nor restored. In Magisk, open Superuser and change the access of TypeFace Droplet from \"Restrict\" to \"Grant\". Other root managers have similar settings, such as the app profile of KernelSU.
The library is empty. Import a TTF, OTF or TTC file.
Aa Gg Rr 0123 あア永字
Family name written into the font
Applications that look fonts up by name (such as Firefox) find the font under this name. Leave empty to keep the original name.
The font file is deleted from the library.
No roles. A role is a set of fonts that replaces system font families.
Values for variation axes other than wght and ital (for example opsz or GRAD), for every face of the role.
The role and every rule that uses it are deleted.
Optional. Overrides the weight of a static font, or pins the wght axis of a variable font.
Fixed axes of this face (override those of the role)
Rules decide which system font families each role replaces. They are tried from the top; the first rule that matches a family decides.
A family name, such as sans-serif. * matches anything and ? matches one character.
A font file name without extension, such as Roboto-*. Named families that use a matching file are replaced.
A BCP 47 language tag, such as ja, matched against the first language of fallback families.
A fallback family made of these roles is inserted before the first matching fallback family. Fallback-for names the generic family (serif, monospace) a font serves.
Choose a role, or a single font. A rule for exactly this family is added first, so it overrides the other rules.
Shizuku must run as root (started with root, or provided by Sui). Shizuku started through ADB cannot apply fonts.
The replacement disappears at every reboot; this applies it again once the system has started.
After a reload, the guard watches the system for this long. If the system crashes, it restores the original fonts at once, and automatic application stays paused.
Running applications keep their fonts. These are restarted after applying or restoring, so that they use the new fonts at once.

Disabled for every user while the fonts are applied, and restored afterwards. By default, the downloadable font provider of Google Play services, so that applications requesting fonts from it (such as Google Sans) use the system fonts.
Generate documents even when their version is newer than this version knows.
Fonts, roles, rules, components and restart targets return to the recommended configuration. Imported fonts stay in the library.
The engine keeps installed fonts in %1$s.
The bundled fonts (Nercone Sans, Serif and Mono CJK NF) are licensed under the SIL Open Font License 1.1.
Before uninstalling, restore the original fonts: that also re-enables the components this application disabled.
